raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not want to toss things around too much. On my 10.1 mu, I will still do wheat after autumn and maize right after wheat harvest, same as most people here. That way the land does not sit empty, and if one crop is not so good, the other can still help the family. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate so finely. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can safely spend. Wheat cannot be too thin on fertilizer or water, otherwise the ears are small. Maize has a tight planting window after wheat, so I will keep it simple, hire machine work where needed, and not do fancy things. I have a well, so I can irrigate, but pumping costs money, so I will use water mainly at the important times.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation on all 10.1 mu because it is the safest for my family and fits our land. I do not want to spend too much at once, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard because low yield hurts more than saving a little money. For wheat I will feed and water it at the key times, because around here good wheat usually needs that. For maize I will plant as soon as wheat is off the field, because if planting is late the yield drops fast.
